p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file defines *how* a campaign's phases are cut, gated, and resumed: the Phase 0 spike discipline, the anatomy of an executable phase, the safe-stop law, review points, and the rule for discovered-necessary work.

p.sibling-document-pointers: The surrounding plan format: [`CAMPAIGN-PLAN-FORMAT.xml`](CAMPAIGN-PLAN-FORMAT.xml); the record half: [`execution-ledger.xml`](execution-ledger.xml).

phase-zero.title: Phase 0 — spikes and probes, no commits

p.EVERY-CAMPAIGN-OPENS-WITH-A-PHASE-THAT-P: Every campaign opens with a phase that produces **no commits**.

p.phase-zeros-job-lead: Its job is to convert the plan's riskiest assumptions into observed facts before anything lands:

facts.PHASE-ZERO-PROBE-THE-ENVIRONMENT: probe the environment the phases depend on,
facts.PHASE-ZERO-SPIKE-THE-ONE-MECHANISM: spike the one mechanism the design leans on,
facts.PHASE-ZERO-RE-MEASURE-THE-NUMBERS: re-measure the numbers the arithmetic trusts,
facts.PHASE-ZERO-VERIFY-WHAT-THE-PLAN-CALLS-IN: verify that whatever the plan calls inert really is inert.

facts.RULE-NO-TREE-CHANGES-SURVIVE-THE-SPIKES: **No tree changes survive the spikes.** Scratch directories, throwaway scripts, temporary workspaces — all discarded. The only durable output is findings, written into the plan itself.
facts.RULE-PHASE-ZERO-GATES-EVERYTHING-AFTER: **Phase 0 gates everything after.** A red spike does not "get noted for later" — it **rewrites the affected Decision in the plan, in place, before Phase 1 commits anything**. The plan is cheap to change while nothing is committed; that is the entire point of spiking first.
facts.RULE-FINDINGS-ARE-RECORDED-EVEN-WHEN-GRE: **Findings are recorded even when green.** The phase's exit is a findings list appended under the phase, not a feeling of readiness. Each finding is marked binding on the phases it affects.

p.the-build-topology-spike: Two real corrections Phase 0 has bought, anonymized: a build-topology spike revealed that a shared engine depended on a fourth component the plan's move-set had not listed — the decision was corrected from "move three" to "move four" before any phase committed to the wrong topology.

p.the-protocol-spike: A protocol spike proved the transport was line-delimited where the draft decision said length-prefixed framing — the decision was rewritten before the transport layer was authored.

p.the-fix-cost-one-edit-not-a-rollback: In both cases the fix cost one edit; discovered in Phase 3, it would have cost a rollback.

anatomy.title: Anatomy of a phase

p.a-phase-carries-four-elements-lead: Every phase after Phase 0 is written as a self-contained executable unit carrying four elements:

td.ROW-ELEMENT-NUMBERED-STEPS-CONTENT: the recipe: commands, paths, exact edits, in order

td.ROW-ELEMENT-EXIT-ACCEPTANCE-CONTENT: the criterion that closes the phase, checkable by command

td.ROW-ELEMENT-COMMIT-SET-CONTENT: the planned commits, subjects spelled in advance

p.worked-phase-lead: A worked phase, condensed from a real campaign:

anatomy.fence:
## 5. Phase 2 — the 24 banned-call sites: convert or testify
Judgment rule per site, in priority order: (a) real fallibility → route through the layer's error type; (b) a true invariant, unreachable by construction → an annotated waiver carrying a reason; (c) test-support code that leaked into production → move it out.
1. Batch 2a — the workspace layer (11 sites, mostly (a)). 2. Batch 2b — the resolver layer (13 sites, prime (b) candidates — "the checker already validated this branch" is a construction invariant).
*Exit:* banned-call findings = 0; every waiver carries a reason a reviewer can argue with. *Prediction:* at least a third of the 24 land as waivers — the ban's value here is the testimony, not the conversion count. *Commits:* `refactor(workspace): route fallible edges through the error type` · `refactor(resolver): waive construction invariants with reasons`.

p.why-subjects-are-spelled-in-advance: Why subjects are spelled in advance: the split of the work into commits-by-meaning happens at planning time, when the whole change is visible.

p.EXECUTION-STAGES-ONTO-A-PRE-DRAWN-MAP: Execution then stages onto a pre-drawn map, and the ledger later binds real hashes to the planned subjects — any drift between the two is itself a recorded finding.

p.ANY-PHASE-BOUNDARY-IS-A-SAFE-STOP: **Any phase boundary is a safe stop, and the project's green floor holds at every boundary.**

p.THE-PANEL-IS-THE-FULL-ONE-NOT-THE-PARTS-: The *full* gate panel — build, verification suite, every standing check — not just the parts the phase touched.

p.A-PHASE-THAT-LEAVES-THE-FLOOR-RED-IS-STI: A phase that leaves the floor red is not done; it is open, whatever its steps say.

facts.BUYS-THE-EXECUTOR-CAN-STOP-AT-ANY-BOUNDA: The executor can stop at any boundary — end of day, session death, an owner interrupt — and leave no broken tree behind.
facts.BUYS-A-FAILED-PHASE-ROLLS-BACK-ALONE: A failed phase rolls back without losing prior phases.
facts.BUYS-PHASES-MUST-BE-CUT-TO-MAKE-THIS-POS: Phases must be *cut* to make this possible: a restructuring that breaks the build across two phases is one phase, not two. If two steps cannot be separated by a green boundary, they are one phase.

p.THE-PLAN-PLUS-THE-LEDGER-ARE-THE-RESUME-: The plan plus its execution ledger are the resume pointer — **no conversational context needed**.

p.a-fresh-session-reads-boot-then-the-plan: A fresh session resumes by reading the project's boot documents, then the plan top to bottom:

facts.RESUME-THE-STATUS-LINE-NAMES-THE-STATE: the status line names the campaign's state,
facts.RESUME-THE-LEDGERS-LAST-ENTRY-NAMES-THE-: the ledger's last entry names the last landed phase,
facts.RESUME-THE-FIRST-UNEXECUTED-PHASE-IS-THE: and the first unexecuted phase is the work.

p.the-journal-points-at-the-plan: If the project keeps a working journal, the campaign updates the journal's standing line at every boundary ("Phase N landed, floor green, next: Phase N+1") and the journal points at the plan; the plan file, not the journal, carries the campaign detail.

p.RESUMPTION-STATE-LIVES-IN-THE-REPOSITORY: Either way the rule is the same: **resumption state lives in the repository, never in a session.**

review-points.title: Review points

p.AN-OWNER-ONLY-DECISION-BECOMES-A-NUMBERE: A decision that only the owner can make — a scope call, a policy reversal, a trade-off between published invariants — becomes a numbered review point instead of a silent executor guess.

p.A-REVIEW-POINT-IS-STATED-OPEN-THEN-ANNOT: It is stated `OPEN` with the options and the executor's recommendation; when the owner rules, it is annotated `RESOLVED` with the ruling **verbatim** and dated, and the affected Decisions are rewritten in place.

p.THE-REVIEW-POINT-KEEPS-THE-HISTORY: The review point keeps the history; the Decisions carry the outcome.

review-points.fence: 3. Package topology — OPEN: one package, or one per language? Executor recommends per-language (skew analysis in D2). → RESOLVED (owner, 2026-07-07, reverses the draft): "make it a separate kind; more kinds may follow later." D1 rewritten in place; consequences surfaced in the amendment discussion.

p.WORK-BLOCKED-ON-AN-OPEN-REVIEW-POINT-DOE: Work that depends on an `OPEN` review point does not start; phases that do not depend on it may proceed.

p.a-reversal-is-normal-not-exceptional: A ruling that reverses a Decision is normal, not exceptional — the format exists so reversals land in the plan, not in a chat scrollback.

p.MID-PHASE-DISCOVERIES-ARE-LEGAL-BUT-RECO: Mid-phase discoveries are **legal but recorded — never done silently "while I was here."**

p.two-dispositions-lead: A discovery has exactly two dispositions:

facts.DISPOSITION-ENTER-THE-CURRENT-PHASE-EXPL: **Enter the current phase explicitly:** a ledger entry naming what was discovered and why it cannot wait, plus its own commit in the phase's commit set.
facts.DISPOSITION-DEFER-BY-NAME: **Defer by name:** a line in the deferrals ledger with an owner and a disposition, drained by a later phase or a later campaign.

p.silent-scope-growth-loses-auditability: Silent scope growth is how campaigns lose auditability: the diff stops mapping to the plan, and the next reader cannot tell the planned from the improvised.

p.EVERY-DEVIATION-LEAVES-A-WRITTEN-TRACE-W: The rule is not "never deviate" — the ledger records deviations precisely because they happen — the rule is that every deviation leaves a written trace at the moment it is made.

facts.SUM-PHASE-ZERO-COMMITS-NOTHING: Phase 0 spikes, probes, and commits nothing; a red spike rewrites the affected Decision before Phase 1 lands a single commit.
facts.SUM-EVERY-LATER-PHASE-CARRIES-FOUR-ELEME: Every later phase carries steps, an exit criterion, its own prediction, and its commit set with subjects spelled in advance.
facts.SUM-ANY-BOUNDARY-IS-A-SAFE-STOP: Any phase boundary is a safe stop; the full gate panel is green at every boundary, or the phase is still open.
facts.SUM-RESUMPTION-STATE-LIVES-IN-THE-REPOSI: The plan plus the ledger are the resume pointer; resumption state lives in the repository, never in a session.
facts.SUM-OWNER-ONLY-DECISIONS-BECOME-REVIEW-P: Owner-only decisions become review points: OPEN, then RESOLVED with the ruling verbatim.
facts.SUM-DISCOVERED-WORK-IS-ENTERED-OR-DEFERR: Discovered work enters the phase explicitly or is deferred by name — never done silently.
